purpose: Time-aware foundation layer for religious traditions. Foundation is an emergence layer, not a claim that a tradition has one simple beginning.

model.field: The wider historical, cultural, ecological, linguistic and political environment already present.
model.substrate: Predecessor traditions, inherited stories, language, institutions, landscape and social structures.
model.seed: The earliest identifiable emergence or formative event-set.
model.sprout: Early community, practice, teachers, texts and places.
model.formation: The period in which a recognizable tradition, authority structure and body of practice crystallize.
model.trunk: Long-term continuity: institutions, canon, ritual, law, philosophy and collective memory.
model.branches: Schools, denominations, geographic forms, reform movements, mystical currents and modern transformations.

records.field: Ancient Near Eastern and Israelite/Judahite religious worlds
records.seed: Long-duration emergence rather than one datable founding event
records.traditional_origin: Biblical and rabbinic traditions connect Jewish origins with ancestors, covenant, exodus, Sinai and Israel
records.historical_emergence: Israelite religion develops in the Iron Age; later rabbinic Judaism takes shape especially after the Second Temple period
formation_markers: First Temple and Second Temple institutions
destruction of the Second Temple in 70 CE
records.uncertainty: High for a single founding date; Judaism is a long historical formation.

records.field: 1st-century Jewish and Roman eastern Mediterranean world
records.seed: Jesus movement in 1st-century Judea and Galilee
records.traditional_origin: Christian traditions center their origin on Jesus, his ministry, death and resurrection
records.uncertainty: Moderate on specific dates and sequence; broad emergence is well established historically.

records.field: 7th-century Arabian world connected to Byzantine, Sasanian, Jewish and Christian environments
records.seed: Muhammad's preaching and the early Muslim community
records.traditional_origin: Islamic tradition centers revelation of the Qur'an to Muhammad
records.uncertainty: Low for broad emergence; some details of earliest chronology remain debated.

records.field: South Asian religious and philosophical field
records.seed: No single seed; multiple interacting formations
records.traditional_origin: Multiple Hindu traditions locate sacred origins in Vedic revelation and ancient teachers
records.historical_emergence: Vedic traditions are attested from the 2nd millennium BCE; the category Hinduism develops much later
records.uncertainty: Very high for a single founding point; best represented as a branching formation.

records.seed: Gautama Buddha and the early sangha
records.traditional_origin: Buddhist traditions center on Siddhartha Gautama's awakening
records.historical_emergence: Conventionally 5th–4th century BCE; exact dates debated
formation_markers: development of Nikaya/Agama and later Mahayana traditions
records.uncertainty: Moderate regarding exact chronology; broad historical emergence is well established.

records.seed: Mahavira's reformative/teaching career within a longer lineage
records.traditional_origin: Jain tradition recognizes a succession of Tirthankaras
records.historical_emergence: Ancient tradition; Mahavira conventionally placed in the 6th century BCE
records.uncertainty: High for earliest lineage history; tradition's own chronology must be preserved separately.

records.seed: Guru Nanak's teaching and the early Sikh community
records.traditional_origin: Sikh tradition centers the revelation and teaching of Guru Nanak and succession of Gurus
formation_markers: Guru Granth Sahib as enduring scripture/guru

records.seed: Zarathustra's teachings within an earlier Iranian religious field
records.traditional_origin: Zoroastrian tradition centers Zarathustra and revelation associated with Ahura Mazda
records.historical_emergence: Ancient; Zarathustra's date remains strongly debated
formation_markers: Achaemenid and later Iranian religious contexts
records.uncertainty: High for dates and early historical reconstruction.

records.field: Warring States and early imperial China
records.seed: Classical Daoist textual traditions associated especially with Laozi and Zhuangzi
records.traditional_origin: Daoist traditions attribute foundational teachings to sages including Laozi
records.historical_emergence: Classical texts from late 1st millennium BCE; organized religious Daoism develops later
formation_markers: Celestial Masters and later religious institutions
records.uncertainty: High for single-founder narratives; textual and institutional histories differ.

records.seed: Confucius and the early Ru scholarly tradition
records.traditional_origin: Tradition centers Confucius as exemplary teacher
records.uncertainty: Moderate; historical Confucius and later Confucianism must not be collapsed.

records.field: Ancient Japanese landscape and ritual communities
records.seed: No single founder; localized ritual systems
records.traditional_origin: Japanese traditions preserve narratives involving kami, imperial ancestors and sacred places
records.historical_emergence: Ancient practices; Shinto as a named modern category crystallizes over later periods
formation_markers: early modern kokugaku and modern state Shinto
records.uncertainty: High for a single origin date.

records.seed: Bábí movement and subsequent emergence of Bahá'u'lláh's community
records.traditional_origin: Bahá'í history centers the Báb and Bahá'u'lláh

records.seed: Multiple regional cults and ritual systems rather than one founder
records.historical_emergence: Predynastic and early dynastic periods; evidence from the 4th–3rd millennia BCE
records.uncertainty: High for a single beginning; strong evidence for gradual institutional formation.
High for one origin; archaeological record supports deep gradual formation.

records.historical_emergence: 2nd millennium BCE onward; classical forms develop in 1st millennium BCE

records.seed: Distributed local and regional cults rather than one founder
records.historical_emergence: Pre-Christian; evidence especially from 1st millennium CE
records.uncertainty: High because much surviving literary evidence is later than the practices described.

records.field: Finnic northern forest, lake and agricultural environments
records.historical_emergence: Pre-Christian; reconstructed through archaeology, folklore and later records
records.uncertainty: High because documentation is late and mediated.

records.seed: Multiple interacting local and regional traditions
records.historical_emergence: Precolonial and long-duration; no single founding date
records.uncertainty: High for a single origin; strong evidence for continuity and transformation.

records.field: The modern digital, cultural and personal field from which the Potatoism project emerged
substrate: Tree of Life / Tree of Strife architecture
records.traditional_origin: Potatoism's own developing narrative may interpret its birth symbolically; this field records the project history rather than validating supernatural claims.
records.historical_emergence: 2020-12-25 as the current declared birth marker
records.development_model: birth -> seed -> sprouting -> symbolic vocabulary -> cosmological architecture -> comparative system -> continuing development
records.uncertainty: The date is a project/self-history marker; later research should distinguish dated artifacts, retrospective interpretation and evolving terminology.

integrity: A foundation may contain multiple beginnings and uncertainty. Never convert a traditional origin story into a historical date without evidence, and never treat the existence of a historical emergence point as the total explanation of a tradition.
